title: Fruit and shoot borer of brinjal - Nepal

Header: Fruit and shoot borer of brinjal - Nepal
Leucinodes orbonalis Bhanta ko phal ra danth ko gabaro

Prevention: Collect and burn plant remnants from the previous crop.
Use tolerant varieties; round- shaped fruit bearing varieties have higher tolerance to this pest, e.g. ‘Pusa purple round’.
It is advisable to plant root crops after solanaceous vegetables.
Intercrop with coriander at proportion of 1 row brinjal: 1 row coriander in the same field.
Synchronize planting dates with neighbouring fields as this can help reduce the intensity of pest infestation.
Monitoring: At the vegetative stage, look for dropping tender shoots and wilting; 2% of plants showing symptoms is the action threshold.
At the fruiting stage, look for holes on fruit filled with insect excreta.
Take control action if a minimum of 1% of fruit show this symptom.
Use water traps/funnel traps with a leucin lure; use 2 traps / ropani and check the traps every morning.
Change the lure septa every 15 days and clean the trap.
Take control action when you observe 5 adult borers in a trap.
Direct Control: Check the field regularly and collect and destroy any infested shoots, twigs, fruits, fallen leaves and fallen fruits.
Azadirachtin (0.03%EC) (neem- based insecticide) at 5ml/L water, and 25L water/ropani.
Trichogramma chilonis once trap thresholds reached; use 2500 parasitoids /ropani, i.e. one ‘tricho-card’.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Use a foliar application of emamectin benzoate (5% SG) at a rate of 2g/16L water, and 25L water /ropani at 15 days intervals.
Use a spray of cypermethrin (10% EC) at 2 ml /L water, and 25L water/ropani).
Spray a maximum of 3 times with 10 days between each spray.
Spray in the early morning or late afternoon.
Cypermethrin kills a number of important natural enemies.
Chlorantraniliprole (18.5 % EC) at 0.4 ml/L water, and 25L water/ropani.
